questions.question:
How many triangles are there in the given figure?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba0f9ee51b9a23568e04ddf07a0c80e54fcb83352d288800a430b89cfe08f2ed.png]
questions.solution:
The number of triangles in the given figure is shown below:

1) Number of triangles = [Number of parts × (1 + Number of parts)] ÷ 2

= [2 × (1 + 2)] ÷ 2

= [2 × 3] ÷ 2

= 6 ÷ 2

= 3

As there are 4 same types of triangles, therefore total number of triangles will be (3 × 4) = 12 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a87bbb89c61a9b6d646fbf90d7c34ebd4f9c72594ab160521d36456d7aacbd3.png] 

2) Number of triangles = 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95467aa111dd697b4845efc214629f0f97b59a4cdc95c629259ad6d16ef1970e.png] 

Thus, there are a total of (12 + 2) = 14 triangles.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option which is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words should be treated as meaningful words in English/Hindi and should not be related to each other on the basis of number of letters/consonants/vowels.)

Library : Catalog :: Restaurant : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic:** Reference tools used in specific places**.

Here,

Library : Catalog → **Catalog** is a reference tool used in a **Library**.

Similarly,

Restaurant : Menu → **Menu** is a reference tool used in a **Restaurant**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

(Note: Mathematical operations should be performed on whole numbers only, without dividing the number into its component digits. questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number ÷ 3rd number)² = 2nd number.

Now,

For, 6 : 9 : 2

⇒ (6 ÷ 2)² = 3² = 9.

For, 12 : 36 : 2

⇒ (12 ÷ 2)² = 6² = 36.

Similarly, for** 18 : 9 : 6**

**⇒ (18 ÷ 6)² = 3² = 9.**

Hence, the co
rrect answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements. 

**Statement: **

Some bottles are windows. 

Some windows are handles. 

All doors are handles.

**Conclusion:**

I. Some bottles are handles.

II. Some windows are bottles.

III. Some doors are bottles.

options.text: Conclusions I, II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bf8b50c2b6afe0c367c76a76faa569846008c0228bf14edc1e799b6510c19d4.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some bottles are handles → Does not follow (As some bottles are windows and some windows are handles. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some windows are bottles → Follow (As some bottles are windows. As some part of bottles are windows, therefore it is true.)

III. Some doors are bottles → Does not follow (As some bottles are windows, some windows are handles and all doors are handles. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion II follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
